newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KLM silent on cargo side of Northwest deal.
newsitem.headline: KLM silent on cargo side of Northwest deal.

text.p: KLM Royal Dutch Airlines has refused so far to give more details of the freight aspects of its tie-up with Northwest Airlines.
Earlier on Wednesday, the two airlines announced that they had agreed in principle on a "far-reaching and long-term" alliance.
In the statement, the airlines said "they will intensify their cooperation in the air freight sector."
But a KLM Cargo spokesman said the two companies will not reveal any details until after the 60-day deadline following discussions between the two carriers.
Transport analyst, Gert Jochems of NIB Securities, expressed little surprise about the announcement.

Dutch financial analysts are not expecting the two airlines to form a separate cargo operation but Jochems said he expects joint purchasing, joint pricing and cross-border selling, each selling one behalf of the other with a joint brand name a possible eventuality.

"It is good to see that KLM has come to its senses. The losses it has had in the cargo department have been partly because of lack of cooperation with other carriers. The alliance with NWAC should enable them to save tens of millions of guilders."
The benefits are evident, he added. "If you are a shipper in China or Japan, a company then has access to a significant share of the European and U.S. market through a single operator."
Synergies also exist he said because KLM has the knowledge of logistics and distribution as the Netherlands is a leader in the field, whereas NWAC has the know how needed for marketing the product.

But he expressed disappointment in the delay because of the court cases concerning the KLM shareholding. "It is a pity as Lufthansa and United have been forging ahead with their alliance and KLM and NWAC were originally the pioneers of these global alliances."
